title: Beginner Pack 8
subtitle: Everyday Questions — Who, What & Where
label: 3 patterns · 6 questions
description: Learn to ask open questions using short question-and-answer exchanges with 何 (なに/なん), どこ, and だれ. Test personal identity, find places, and understand conversational responses.
sources: Komorebi original conversational exchanges for everyday beginner Japanese
JLPT N5 Interrogatives Reference: 何 (741#2), どこ (741#3), だれ (741#4)

patterns.readingNote: Before です, 何 is read as なん (nan), not なに.
patterns.summary: In Japanese, question words slot directly into the sentence where the answer would go. To ask what something is, use 何 (なん) with the polite copula and question particle: 何ですか (nan desu ka). In conversation, this appears in short question-and-answer exchanges.

examples.japanese: 「これは何ですか。」「日本語の本です。」
examples.reading: 「これは なんですか。」「にほんごの ホンです。」
examples.gloss: これ this · 何 what · 日本語 Japanese language · 本 book
examples.english: “What is this?” “It is a Japanese book.”

examples.japanese: 「あれは何ですか。」「駅の入り口です。」
examples.reading: 「あれは なんですか。」「えきの いりぐち です。」
examples.gloss: あれ that over there · 何 what · 駅 station · 入り口 entrance
examples.english: “What is that over there?” “It is the station entrance.”

questions.prompt: In this short exchange, what is Speaker A asking?
questions.japanese: 「これは何ですか。」「日本語の本です。」
questions.reading: 「これは なんですか。」「にほんごの ほんです。」
questions.gloss: これ this · 何 what · 日本語 Japanese language · 本 book

choices.text: Speaker A asks what the item is, and Speaker B answers that it is a Japanese book.
choices.explanation: That’s right! 何ですか (nan desu ka) asks “what is it?”, and Speaker B identifies the object as a Japanese book.

choices.text: Speaker A asks who wrote the book, and Speaker B says they are Japanese.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 何 (nan) asks “what,” not “who” (だれ, dare), so the question asks what the item is.

choices.text: Speaker A asks where the bookstore is, and Speaker B points to Japan.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 何 asks “what,” not “where” (どこ, doko).

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this new exchange mean?
followUp.japanese: 「あれは何ですか。」「駅の入り口です。」
followUp.reading: 「あれは なんですか。」「えきの いりぐち です。」
followUp.gloss: あれ that over there · 何 what · 駅 station · 入り口 entrance

choices.text: “Where is the station?” “That over there is an entrance.”
choices.explanation: Not quite. あれは何ですか asks “what is that over there?”, not where the station is.

choices.text: “What is that over there?” “It is the station entrance.”
choices.explanation: That’s right! あれは何ですか (are wa nan desu ka) asks what the distant structure is, and Speaker B identifies it as the station entrance.

choices.text: “Who is at the station?” “An entrance worker.”
choices.explanation: Not quite. 何 asks “what,” not “who” (だれ).

workedExample.japanese: 「あれは何ですか。」「駅の入り口です。」
workedExample.reading: 「あれは なんですか。」「えきの いりぐち です。」
workedExample.english: “What is that over there?” “It is the station entrance.”
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: あれ (“that over there”) + は sets the distant object as the topic. Step 2: 何 (read なん before です) + ですか asks “what is it?”. Step 3: 駅の入り口です identifies the object as “the station entrance.”

questions.prompt: Complete the question to ask “What is in that box?”:
questions.japanese: 「その箱の中は（　）ですか。」「お茶です。」
questions.targetMeaning: “What is inside that box?” “It is tea.”
questions.reading: 「その はこの なかは（　）ですか。」「おちゃ です。」
questions.gloss: その箱 that box · 中 inside · お茶 tea

choices.text: どこ
choices.explanation: Not quite. どこ asks “where,” but Speaker B answers with an object (お茶, tea), so the question requires “what” (何 / なん).

choices.text: 何
choices.explanation: That’s right! 何 (read なん before です) asks “what,” perfectly matching the answer お茶です (“It is tea”).

choices.text: だれ
choices.explanation: Not quite. だれ asks “who” for people, not “what” for objects in a box.

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Complete the question asking what the person is drinking:
followUp.japanese: 「その飲み物は（　）ですか。」「冷たい水です。」
followUp.targetMeaning: “What is that drink?” “It is cold water.”
followUp.reading: 「その のみものは（　）ですか。」「つめたい みず です。」
followUp.gloss: その飲み物 that beverage · 冷たい水 cold water

choices.text: どこ
choices.explanation: Not quite. どこ asks “where,” but the response names a drink (冷たい水, cold water).

choices.text: だれ
choices.explanation: Not quite. だれ asks “who” for a person.

choices.text: 何
choices.explanation: That’s right! 何 (read なん before です) asks “what,” which matches the answer 冷たい水です (“It is cold water”).

workedExample.japanese: 「その飲み物は何ですか。」「冷たい水です。」
workedExample.reading: 「その のみものは なんですか。」「つめたい みず です。」
workedExample.english: “What is that drink?” “It is cold water.”
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: その飲み物は sets “that drink” as the topic. Step 2: To ask what kind of drink it is, insert 何 (read なん before です). Step 3: Result: その飲み物は何ですか (“What is that drink?”).

patterns.readingNote: どこ (doko) asks for a place or location.
patterns.summary: To ask where a person, building, or room is located, place the topic first and follow with どこですか (doko desu ka). The response typically points to a location, a landmark, or uses directional demonstratives (ここ here, そこ there, あそこ over there).

examples.japanese: 「駅の入り口はどこですか。」「あそこです。」
examples.reading: 「えきの いりぐちは どこですか。」「あそこ です。」
examples.gloss: 駅の入り口 station entrance · どこ where · あそこ over there
examples.english: “Where is the station entrance?” “It is over there.”

examples.japanese: 「あなたの部屋はどこですか。」「二階です。」
examples.reading: 「あなたの へやは どこですか。」「にかい です。」
examples.gloss: あなたの部屋 your room · どこ where · 二階 second floor
examples.english: “Where is your room?” “It is on the second floor.”

questions.prompt: Choose the question word that asks for the location of the station entrance:
questions.japanese: 「駅の入り口は（　）ですか。」「あそこです。」
questions.targetMeaning: “Where is the station entrance?” “It is over there.”
questions.reading: 「えきの いりぐちは（　）ですか。」「あそこ です。」
questions.gloss: 駅の入り口 station entrance · あそこ over there

choices.text: 何
choices.explanation: Not quite. 何 (nan) asks “what,” but Speaker B answers with a place (あそこ, over there).

choices.text: だれ
choices.explanation: Not quite. だれ asks “who” for a person, not “where” for a location.

choices.text: どこ
choices.explanation: That’s right! どこ (doko) asks “where,” perfectly matching the location answer あそこです (“It is over there”).

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Complete the question asking for the hotel's location:
followUp.japanese: 「あのホテルは（　）ですか。」「川の近くです。」
followUp.targetMeaning: “Where is that hotel?” “It is near the river.”
followUp.reading: 「あの ホテルは（　）ですか。」「かわの ちかく です。」
followUp.gloss: ホテル hotel · 川の近く near the river

choices.text: どこ
choices.explanation: That’s right! どこ (doko) asks “where,” matching Speaker B’s location answer 川の近くです (“It is near the river”).

choices.text: 何
choices.explanation: Not quite. 何 asks “what,” but Speaker B answers with a physical location.

choices.text: だれ
choices.explanation: Not quite. だれ asks “who” for a person.

workedExample.japanese: 「あのホテルはどこですか。」「川の近くです。」
workedExample.reading: 「あの ホテルは どこですか。」「かわの ちかく です。」
workedExample.english: “Where is that hotel?” “It is near the river.”
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: あのホテルは establishes the hotel as the topic. Step 2: To ask for its location, add どこですか. Step 3: Result: あのホテルはどこですか (“Where is that hotel?”).

questions.prompt: What does this conversational exchange mean?
questions.japanese: 「あなたの部屋はどこですか。」「二階の明るい部屋です。」
questions.reading: 「あなたの へやは どこですか。」「にかいの あかるい へや です。」
questions.gloss: あなたの部屋 your room · どこ where · 二階 second floor · 明るい部屋 bright room

choices.text: “Who is in your room?” “Two bright people.”
choices.explanation: Not quite. どこ asks “where,” not “who” (だれ), and 二階 means “second floor,” not two people.

choices.text: “Where is your room?” “It is the bright room on the second floor.”
choices.explanation: That’s right! どこですか asks for the room’s location, and Speaker B explains that it is the bright room on the second floor.

choices.text: “What is inside your room?” “A bright light on the floor.”
choices.explanation: Not quite. どこ asks “where is your room,” not what is inside it (何がありますか).

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this new exchange mean?
followUp.japanese: 「お手洗いはどこですか。」「あそこですよ。」
followUp.reading: 「おてあらいは どこですか。」「あそこ ですよ。」
followUp.gloss: お手洗い restroom · どこ where · あそこ over there

choices.text: “What is over there?” “It is the washroom, you know.”
choices.explanation: Not quite. The question asks お手洗いはどこですか (“Where is the restroom?”), not what is over there.

choices.text: “Who is in the washroom?” “Someone over there.”
choices.explanation: Not quite. どこ asks “where,” not “who” (だれ).

choices.text: “Where is the restroom?” “It is right over there, you know.”
choices.explanation: That’s right! お手洗いはどこですか asks for the restroom location, and Speaker B helpfully points it out.

workedExample.japanese: 「お手洗いはどこですか。」「あそこですよ。」
workedExample.reading: 「おてあらいは どこですか。」「あそこ ですよ。」
workedExample.english: “Where is the restroom?” “It is right over there, you know.”
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: お手洗いは sets “the restroom” as the topic. Step 2: どこですか asks for its location. Step 3: あそこですよ politely indicates the location with informational particle よ.

patterns.readingNote: だれ (dare) asks for a person's identity or role.
patterns.summary: To ask for a person's identity, name, or role, use だれですか (dare desu ka). Unlike asking 'what kind of person' (which might describe age or gender), だれ asks specifically who someone is, and the response provides their name (e.g. 田中さん), role (e.g. 先生), or relationship (e.g. 友だち).

examples.japanese: 「あの人はだれですか。」「日本語の田中先生です。」
examples.reading: 「あの ひとは だれですか。」「にほんごの たなか せんせい です。」
examples.gloss: あの人 that person · だれ who · 田中先生 Teacher Tanaka
examples.english: “Who is that person?” “That is Tanaka-sensei, the Japanese teacher.”

examples.japanese: 「この男の人はだれですか。」「私の友だちです。」
examples.reading: 「この おとこの ひとは だれですか。」「わたしの ともだち です。」
examples.gloss: この男の人 this man · だれ who · 私の友だち my friend
examples.english: “Who is this man?” “He is my friend.”

questions.prompt: What does this exchange establish about the person over there?
questions.japanese: 「あの人はだれですか。」「日本語の田中先生です。」
questions.reading: 「あの ひとは だれですか。」「にほんごの たなか せんせい です。」
questions.gloss: あの人 that person · だれ who · 日本語 Japanese · 田中先生 Teacher Tanaka

choices.text: Speaker A asks where Tanaka-sensei is going, and Speaker B says to Japan.
choices.explanation: Not quite. だれ asks “who,” not “where” (どこ).

choices.text: Speaker A asks what Tanaka-sensei is reading, and Speaker B says a Japanese book.
choices.explanation: Not quite. The question asks だれですか (“who is that person?”), inquiring about identity.

choices.text: Speaker A asks who that person is, and Speaker B identifies them as Tanaka-sensei, the Japanese teacher.
choices.explanation: That’s right! だれ (dare) specifically asks for someone’s identity, and Speaker B names Tanaka-sensei and their role.

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this new exchange ask and answer?
followUp.japanese: 「この男の人はだれですか。」「私の友だちの木村さんです。」
followUp.reading: 「この おとこの ひとは だれですか。」「わたしの ともだちの きむらさん です。」
followUp.gloss: この男の人 this man · だれ who · 私の友だち my friend · 木村さん Kimura-san

choices.text: “Who is this man?” “He is my friend, Kimura-san.”
choices.explanation: That’s right! だれですか asks who the man is, and Speaker B identifies him by his relationship (友だち) and name (木村さん).

choices.text: “Where did this man go?” “To Kimura-san's house.”
choices.explanation: Not quite. だれ asks “who,” not “where” (どこ).

choices.text: “What is this man doing?” “Talking with Kimura-san.”
choices.explanation: Not quite. The question asks だれですか (“who is he?”), not what he is doing.

workedExample.japanese: 「この男の人はだれですか。」「私の友だちの木村さんです。」
workedExample.reading: 「この おとこの ひとは だれですか。」「わたしの ともだちの きむらさん です。」
workedExample.english: “Who is this man?” “He is my friend, Kimura-san.”
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: この男の人は sets “this man” as the topic. Step 2: だれですか asks for his personal identity. Step 3: 私の友だちの木村さんです identifies him as “my friend Kimura-san.”

questions.prompt: Complete the question to ask for the person's identity:
questions.japanese: 「あの女の人は（　）ですか。」「英語の先生の山田さんです。」
questions.targetMeaning: “Who is that woman?” “She is Yamada-san, the English teacher.”
questions.reading: 「あの おんなの ひとは（　）ですか。」「えいごの せんせいの やまださん です。」
questions.gloss: あの女の人 that woman · 英語 English · 先生 teacher · 山田さん Yamada-san

choices.text: だれ
choices.explanation: That’s right! だれ (dare) asks “who,” which matches Speaker B’s answer identifying the woman by name and role (山田さん, English teacher).

choices.text: 何
choices.explanation: Not quite. 何 (nan) asks “what,” which is used for objects, not for asking a person’s identity.

choices.text: どこ
choices.explanation: Not quite. どこ asks “where,” but Speaker B answers with a person’s identity, not a location.

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Complete the question asking who is entering the building:
followUp.japanese: 「今ビルに入った人は（　）ですか。」「田中さんです。」
followUp.targetMeaning: “Who was the person that entered the building just now?” “It was Tanaka-san.”
followUp.reading: 「いま ビルに はいった ひとは（　）ですか。」「たなかさん です。」
followUp.gloss: 今 just now · ビル building · 入った entered · 田中さん Tanaka-san

choices.text: どこ
choices.explanation: Not quite. どこ asks “where,” but Speaker B answers with a person’s name (田中さん).

choices.text: だれ
choices.explanation: That’s right! だれ (dare) asks “who,” correctly matching the answer naming Tanaka-san.

choices.text: 何
choices.explanation: Not quite. 何 asks “what,” which is used for things, not people.

workedExample.japanese: 「今ビルに入った人はだれですか。」「田中さんです。」
workedExample.reading: 「いま ビルに はいった ひとは だれですか。」「たなかさん です。」
workedExample.english: “Who was the person that entered the building just now?” “It was Tanaka-san.”
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: 今ビルに入った人は sets “the person who entered the building just now” as the topic. Step 2: To ask who that person is, use だれですか. Step 3: Result: …人はだれですか (“Who was the person…?”).
